newsitem.title: UK: SocGen sets up UK fund arm, talking to Horlick.
newsitem.headline: SocGen sets up UK fund arm, talking to Horlick.

text.p: Societe Generale Asset Management (SGAM) said on Wednesday it was setting up a UK fund management arm to be headed by Mercury Asset Management Plc senior fund manager John Richards.
It also said it was talking to Nicola Horlick, former star fund manager at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, about joining the new team.

SGAM chairman and chief executive officer Phillipe Collas said the new arm was well placed to build an asset management presence in the UK due to its extensive international network and capital strength.
"With John's appointment we look forward to building a team with the skills and experience to develop a major asset management presence for SocGen in the UK market," he said in a statement.
"This new company (Societe Generale Asset Management UK Ltd) will reinforce the core strategy of increasing SGAM's institutional focus and developing its international business," the statement added.

Socgen Asset Management is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SocGen with 500 billion francs ($87.1 billion) under management and operations in ten countries. It has a 10 percent market share in asset management in France but a limited international presence.
Its stated objective is to strengthen its operation in Europe and the UK is a key element in this strategy.
Horlick resigned as head of MGAM's British pension fund business earlier this year from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, owned by Deutsche Bank AG.
She resigned after being suspended for allegedly trying to take her team with her in a defection to Dutch financial services group ABN AMRO.
A spokeswoman confirmed that SocGen was talking to Horlick about joining the team, but said nothing had been settled yet. She could not give a timeframe for the conclusion of negotiations.

SocGen is a major player in fund management in its home country of France but has limited presence internationally, and is seen needing to set up a strong UK presence if it is to build a strong international business.
Richards and Horlick worked together at Mercury, which they joined at the same time. Richards has been with Mercury for 14 years, and Horlick moved to Morgan Grenfell in 1991.
Richards was head of UK institutions and chairman of the UK institutional asset management committee at MAM.
Horlick was not available for comment.
